sessions.title: Marketing Decisions and AI-Assisted Coding
sessions.python_activity: Implement and assess order aggregation; record model, input, parser, and scoring versions. Recompute the synthetic recommendation in optional follow-up practice. Distinguish cancellation events, definitions, and evidence. Compare task information and development feedback on the fixed mHealth logging roster. Reconstruct an AI-assisted recommendation through five argument steps and identify a condition for revision. Examine the worth of the objective, empirical representation, and Kantian limits alongside practical justification. Identify who chooses the objective and which duties govern the analyst’s judgment. Explain how disciplinary institutions shape the choice of analytical questions.

sessions.title: Experiments and Incremental Value
sessions.python_activity: Reproduce experiment calculations and specify purchase, return, and cancellation outcomes. Compare customer-row and store-mean tests under a known zero effect. Calculate prompt effects on additive and proportional-failure scales. Compare naive and population-weighted pricing contrasts under unequal exposure. Compare exact normal error probabilities and expected loss under two opposing cost specifications.
sessions.application: Compare fixed and adaptive research designs, treatment effects, AI-generated proposals, and customer outcomes. Interpret the information-by-feedback interaction at a fixed model version. Store assignment, shared shocks, false positives, and Monte Carlo uncertainty. A workflow comparison changes the opportunity to execute, revise, and verify. Statistical detection versus profit, table-based power, and unsupported mechanism interpretations. Inverse power (Andrews, 1989) and nuisance-parameter sensitivity. Compare observationally equivalent price models and specify the randomized cells that distinguish them. Compare Type I and Type II errors under explicit, asymmetric loss specifications.
sessions.ethics: Defensible treatment designs and informed customer choice; meaningful harms left unresolved by a weak test. Compare the individual reasons for accepting experimental risk.

sessions.title: Generative AI, Consumer Choice, and Regulation
sessions.python_activity: Compare synthetic pricing objectives and signal accuracy, then evaluate customer incidence and renewal. Use the optional Digital Usage lab for the complete geographic analysis. Explain the scope of a joint advertising test and the further evidence needed for welfare. Calculate the hypothetical break-even loss for additional review.
sessions.application: Evaluate customer outcomes, public claims, and institutional duties through Kantian, Confucian, and Scanlonian arguments. Compare stakeholder reasons and opportunities to contest evidence. Personalized pricing, demand completions, mobile targeting (Dubé et al., 2017), and antitrust proof with Scanlonian reasons. Compare rational acceptance with reasonable rejection across pricing and infrastructure reassurance, holding factual estimates fixed. Test definitions, counterfactual premises, welfare valuations, and the strongest reply to an electricity or pricing criticism. Examine the worth of the objective, empirical representation, and Kantian limits alongside practical justification. Assess the ontological spectrum and critiques of empiricism through a selected case; extended source comparisons remain optional practice. Compare conflicts of interest, reward-learning evidence, and consumer control through the synthetic feed case and Kantian, Scanlonian, and Confucian arguments. Bad controls, phantom-project exposure, and thoughtful sample design. Evaluate data as artifacts, truth and norms, undone science, and institutional duties to produce evidence. Evaluate evidentiary standards through conceptual engineering, error costs, and reasonable objections.
sessions.ethics: Kantian and Confucian conduct; Scanlonian reasons and reasonable rejection; stakeholder standing, public voice, and truthful claims. Reasonable rejection, pricing authority, antitrust evidence, and access to critical replication.; measurement quality, worthy objectives, and reasonableness across pricing and data-center claims
